Frazier II''' (born March 8, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Taipei Taishin Mars]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. ==College career== In the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]], Frazier scored eleven [[Three-point field goal|three-pointers]] in a win against [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], setting a school record.{{Cite web |title= Michael Frazier II sets Florida 3-point record as Gators trounce Gamecocks | work = FoxSports.com | date = March 4, 2014| url = http://www.foxsports.com/florida/story/michael-frazier-ii-sets-florida-3-point-record-as-gators-trounce-gamecocks-030414 | access-date = February 19, 2015}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400506456|title=Michael Frazier II scores 37 on 11 3-pointers to power Florida|access-date=May 23, 2015|date=March 4, 2014}} He also set a school record for made three-pointers in a season (118).{{cite news|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/03/27/reports-michael-frazier-ii-will-declare-for-the-nba-draft/|title= 20 Michael Frazier II |work=NBCSports.com|access-date=August 26, 2015}} His junior season was derailed significantly by a high-ankle sprain suffered in the game against [[2014–15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].{{cite news|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/03/27/reports-michael-frazier-ii-will-declare-for-the-nba-draft/|title= Florida junior Michael Frazier II declares for 2015 NBA Draft |work=NBCSports.com|date=March 27, 2015|access-date=August 26, 2015}} On March 27, 2015, Frazier declared his eligibility for the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |title= Florida's Frazier makes it official, declares for NBA draft | work = FoxSports.com | date = March 27, 2015| url = http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/florida-gators-michael-frazier-officially-declares-for-nba-draft-032715 | access-date = March 28, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===NBA D-League and Summer League (2015–2016)=== After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Frazier joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2015/7/21/9000519/michael-frazier-scouting-report-warriors-nba-draft-summer-league|title=Why Michael Frazier could be the NBA's next undrafted sleeper|work=SBNation.com|date=July 21, 2015|access-date=August 26, 2015}} On August 25, 2015, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150817_frazierSigns|title=Lakers Sign Michael Frazier|work=NBA.com|date=August 25, 2015|access-date=August 26, 2015}} However, he was later waived by the Lakers on October 20 after appearing in four preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/151020_frazierUpshaw|title=Lakers Waive Frazier II and Upshaw|work=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2015|access-date=October 20, 2015}} On October 31, he was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Lakers.{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065520|title=D-Fenders Finalize 2015 Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2015|access-date=October 31, 2015}} On November 24, he made his professional debut in a 94–90 win over the [[Oklahoma City Blue]], recording three points, two rebounds and one assist in four minutes.{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151124/LADOKL/|title=Blue Come Up Short To D-Fenders|work=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2015|access-date=February 3, 2016}} On January 16, 2016, Frazier was traded to the [[Iowa Energy]] in exchange for a 2016 second-round pick and the returning player rights to [[Kendrick Perry]].{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-energy-acquire-michael-frazier-from-los-angeles/n-5090549|title=Iowa Energy Acquire Michael Frazier from Los Angeles|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 16, 2016|access-date=January 16, 2016}} Two days later, he made his debut for Iowa in a 98–94 loss to [[Raptors 905]], recording one assist and one steal in nine minutes.{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160118/RAPIWA/|title=Roberts Leads Raptors Past Energy|work=NBA.com|date=January 18, 2016|access-date=February 3, 2016}} On March 6, he was waived by Iowa.{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |title=NBA D-League Transactions |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 9, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309163514/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=March 9, 2016 }} On March 10, 2016, Frazier was acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/mad-ants-acquire-michael-frazier/n-5109447|title=Mad Ants Acquire Michael Frazier|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 10, 2016|access-date=March 10, 2016}} The next day, he made his debut for Fort Wayne in a 106–99 loss to the [[Westchester Knicks]], recording three points in 12 minutes off the bench.{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160311/WESFWN/|title=Fredette Scores 21 to Help Knicks Stomp Out Mad Ants|work=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016}} In July 2016, Frazier played for the [[Orlando Magic]] at the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Michael-Frazier/Summary/24284|title=Michael Frazier|work=realgm.com|access-date=October 14, 2021}} ===Scaligera Basket Verona (2016–2017)=== On August 9, 2016, Frazier signed with [[Scaligera Basket Verona]] of the Italian [[Serie A2 Basket|Serie A2 Citroën]].{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a2-est/209141/michael-frazier-ii-inks-with-verona.html|title=Michael Frazier II inks with Verona|work=Sportando.com|date=August 9, 2016|access-date=September 24, 2016}} ===MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg (2017)=== On June 27, 2017, Frazier signed with German club [[MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]].{{cite news|title=Michael Frazier joins MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/238642/michael-frazier-joins-mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.html|access-date=June 27, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=June 27, 2017}} However, on August 12, 2017, Ludwigsburg voided Frazier's contract{{cite news|title=MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg voids Michael Frazier's contract due to an injury|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/244168/mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg-voids-michael-frazier-s-contract-due-to-an-injury.html|access-date=August 12, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=August 12, 2017}} after he suffered a potential career-ending quad injury.{{cite news|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|title=Perth Wildcats import Michael Frazier II reveals how close he came to never playing again|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/perth-wildcats-import-michael-frazier-ii-reveals-how-close-he-came-to-never-playing-again-c-4446083|access-date=November 7, 2021|work=TheWest.com.au|date=November 7, 2021}} ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2018–2019)=== In October 2018, Frazier joined the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Rio Grande Valley Vipers Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/rio-grande-valley-vipers-finalize-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2018|access-date=October 21, 2018}} In 45 games during the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]], he averaged 16.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 1.5 steals.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/f/frazimi01d.html|title=Michael Frazier G-League Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=April 7, 2019}} He was named the [[NBA G League Most Improved Player Award|G League's Most Improved Player]]{{Cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/michael-frazier-most-improved-player-award-vipers/|title=Rio Grande Valley's Michael Frazier Named 2018–19 NBA G League Most Improved Player|website=NBA G League|language=en-US|access-date=April 7, 2019}} and helped the Vipers win the [[List of NBA G League champions|G League championship]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-g-league/game?gameId=401125919|title=Rio Grande Valley vs. Long Island – Game Summary – April 12, 2019 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=April 13, 2019}} In game three of the Finals series against the [[Long Island Nets]], he scored 24 points with nine rebounds, six assists, two steals and a block in 45 minutes.{{cite web|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/rio-grande-valley-vipers-earn-third-nba-g-league-championship/|title=RIO GRANDE VALLEY VIPERS EARN THIRD NBA G LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP|website=gleague.nba.com|date=April 13, 2019|access-date=October 14, 2021}} === Houston Rockets (2019–2020) === On April 6, 2019, Frazier signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/espn_macmahon/status/1114618480035270656?s=20|title=Source: The Rockets are signing guard Michael Frazier, who was named the G League's Most Improved Player this season. He averaged 16.9 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.4 assists for Rockets affiliate Rio Grande Valley.|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|date=April 6, 2019|website=@espn_macmahon|language=en|access-date=April 7, 2019}}{{Cite web|url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2019/04/06/report-rockets-to-sign-guard-michael-frazier/|title=Report: Rockets to sign guard Michael Frazier|date=April 6, 2019|website=Rockets Wire|language=en|access-date=April 7, 2019}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-michael-frazier|title=Rockets Sign Michael Frazier|website=Houston Rockets|language=en|access-date=April 7, 2019}} He did not play for the Rockets to complete to the [[2018–19 NBA season]]. Frazier was released by the Rockets on October 18, 2019, but was re-signed to a [[two-way contract]] two days later.{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/HoustonRockets/status/1186051880151109633|title=🚀 Roster Update: The Rockets have signed...|website=Twitter|access-date=October 20, 2019}} He split the [[2019–20 NBA season]] with the Rockets and Vipers. ===Delaware Blue Coats (2021)=== In January 2021, Frazier joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] for the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|G League hub season]]. In August 2021, Frazier played for the [[Phoenix Suns]] at the [[2021 NBA Summer League]]. ===Perth Wildcats (2021–2022)=== On October 15, 2021, Frazier signed with the [[Perth Wildcats]] in Australia for the [[2021–22 NBL season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/wildcats-add-more-nba-experience-in-michael-frazier-ii|title=Wildcats add more NBA experience in Michael Frazier II|work=wildcats.com.au|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021}} ===Illawarra Hawks (2022–2023)=== On November 21, 2022, Frazier signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] in Australia for the rest of the [[2022–23 NBL season]].{{cite web|title=Frazier II Answers the Hawks Call|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/frazier-ii-answers-the-hawks-call|website=Hawks.com.au|date=November 21, 2022|access-date=November 21, 2022}} On January 6, 2023, he sustained a severe arm injury in a game against the [[Adelaide 36ers]].{{cite web|title=Hawks Can't Catch a Break Against 36ers|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/hawks-cant-catch-a-break-against-36ers|website=Hawks.com.au|date=January 6, 2023|access-date=January 6, 2023}} He was subsequently ruled out for the rest of the season.{{cite web|title=Michael Frazier II Injury Update|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/michael-frazier-ii-injury-update|website=Hawks.com.au|date=January 8, 2023|access-date=January 8, 2023}} He averaged 17.5 points in eight games for the Hawks. Frazier signed with French team [[Metropolitans 92]] following the NBL season,{{cite web|title=Michael Frazier II pigiste médical pour Hugo Besson|url=https://www.metropolitans92.com/fr/actualites/2023-03-18/pigiste-michael-frazier-ii-pigiste-medical-pour-hugo-besson|website=Metropolitans92.com|date=March 18, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023|language=fr}} but never debuted for the team.{{cite web |last1=Pantel-Jouve |first1=Gabriel |title=Barry Brown Jr. chez les Metropolitans 92, Hugo Besson de retour |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/barry-brown-jr-chez-les-metropolitans-92-hugo-besson-de-retour/ |website=BeBasket |access-date=December 31, 2024 |date=May 15, 2023}} In June 2023, Frazier joined the [[Shandong Hi-Speed Kirin]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] and trained with the team,{{cite web |title=又一个“迈克尔”!“全美最准大学生”加盟山东男篮 |url=http://www.readmeok.com/wt/2023/0616/115858.html |website=读我网 |access-date=December 31, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241231044922/http://www.readmeok.com/wt/2023/0616/115858.html |archive-date=December 31, 2024 |date=June 16, 2023}} but the contract was not signed due to procedural issues.{{cite web |title=马库斯·福斯特签约山东男篮 |url=http://www.readmeok.com/wt/2023/0818/126078.html |website=读我网 |access-date=December 31, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241222001450/http://www.readmeok.com/wt/2023/0818/126078.html |archive-date=December 22, 2024 |date=August 18, 2023}} ===Sichuan Blue Whales (2023)=== On November 3, 2023, Frazier signed with the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.{{cite web |title=四川男篮官宣新外援 格雷格·门罗和迈克尔·弗雷泽加盟 |url=https://cbgc.scol.com.cn/news/4538284 |website=川观新闻 |access-date=December 31, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241231045126/https://cbgc.scol.com.cn/news/4538284 |archive-date=December 31, 2024 |date=November 3, 2023}} On December 5, he was removed from roster after three games.{{cite web |title=CBA官方更新外援注册信息：四川取消门罗和迈克尔-弗雷泽的注册 |url=https://news.zhibo8.com/nba/2023-12-06/656fdab514e42native.htm |website=直播吧 |access-date=December 31, 2024 |date=December 6, 2023}} ===NBA G League Ignite (2024)=== On January 10, 2024, Frazier signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web|title=Ignite Signs NBA G League Champion Michael Frazier II|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/ignite-signs-nba-g-league-champion-michael-frazier-ii|website=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2024|access-date=January 14, 2024}} ===Amman United (2024–2025)=== In December 2024, Frazier joined [[Amman United]] of the [[Jordanian Premier Basketball League]].{{cite news |title=Amman United adds Frazier II to their roster |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Jordan/news/909665/Amman-United-adds-Frazier-II-to-their-roster |access-date=December 31, 2024 |work=asia-basket.com |date=December 30, 2024}} ===Taipei Taishin Mars
